instruction: You are a strategic corporate innovation advisor. Analyse the company profile and survey responses, then respond ONLY with a valid JSON object containing maturity_score, opportunities, next_steps, and key_weaknesses.

answers.companyDescription: Meridian Corporation is a prominent fashion and apparel retail chain operating 45 physical stores across three key shopping regions. Utilizing a fast-fashion model with a rapid six-week design-to-shelf cycle, the company faces intense margin pressure from agile online competitors. They are strategically exploring near-shoring production to mitigate logistics risks and implementing RFID-based inventory visibility systems to significantly improve replenishment speed.
answers.pastInitiatives: We successfully deployed a new CRM system across the sales team 18 months ago, which improved lead tracking and reduced pipeline data entry time by 30%. The implementation was well-planned with dedicated project management and training. Building on this success, we are now exploring marketing automation integration and AI-assisted lead scoring to enhance B2C personalization.
answers.strategicGoals: We are heavily dependent on a single product category and a concentrated customer base — our top 3 clients represent 55% of revenue. This concentration risk is unacceptable for our long-term health. We need to identify and develop new revenue streams, possibly including new product lines for different customer segments or entirely new business models that leverage our existing capabilities.
answers.additionalContext: Meridian is currently tracking a shift toward sustainable materials and experiential retail, requiring investment in new technology to meet evolving consumer demands. The internal organization faces resistance when shifting from proven incremental projects to higher-risk diversification initiatives.
answers.teamSize: Our digital and innovation organization includes 80+ professionals across centers of excellence for AI/ML, cloud engineering, UX design, and agile delivery. We run an internal incubator program that has graduated 6 new digital products to market in the past 2 years, alongside a corporate venture capital arm that makes strategic minority investments in relevant startups.

opportunities.title: AI-Driven Demand Forecasting for Inventory Optimization
opportunities.rationale: Leveraging the existing AI/ML talent pool, implementing advanced predictive analytics can drastically improve inventory turnover and reduce waste in the 6-week cycle. This provides immediate ROI by optimizing existing operations without fundamentally changing the business model.

first_actions: Pilot ML model on Q4 seasonal SKU demand
Integrate forecast outputs into ERP system
execution_plan.success_metric: Reduction in inventory carrying costs by 12% within one fiscal year

opportunities.title: B2B Wholesale Subscription Box Service (Diversification)
opportunities.rationale: Develop a secondary, high-margin revenue stream by transforming existing apparel expertise into a B2B service. This involves creating curated, high-end wholesale subscription boxes targeting boutique retailers or offices, effectively diversifying away from the volatile direct-to-consumer model.

first_actions: Establish R&D for 3 distinct wholesale collection lines
Develop a tiered pricing and logistics framework
execution_plan.success_metric: Achieve $5M in recurring B2B subscription revenue by Year 3
milestones: Collection launch and initial wholesale partnerships (Month 12)

next_steps.action: Form a cross-functional task force (Strategy, Ops, Digital) to map the feasibility and required budget for the B2B Wholesale Subscription concept.
Implement the first phase of the AI demand forecasting pilot in the North American store network to demonstrate incremental value and build internal buy-in against cultural inertia.
Develop a detailed diversification roadmap outlining three potential new product categories or business models outside the current single product category dependency.

key_weaknesses: Strategic alignment is weak across divisions, leading to slow adoption of cross-functional initiatives (culture barrier).
High organizational inertia and resistance to radical diversification models due to a reliance on successful incremental projects.
Partial innovation process makes it difficult to scale successful internal products efficiently beyond the incubator stage.
Concentration risk remains high; lack of strong pipeline for new, unrelated revenue streams.
